headline: GOLD CRATERS TO $4,564; SILVER SHEDS $9 IN ONE SESSION AS HOT INFLATION DATA KILLS RATE-CUT HOPES
snippet: Gold tumbled to $4,564/oz on May 15 — heading for its worst weekly loss since March — as April CPI printed 3.8% YoY and PPI posted its steepest monthly spike since 2022, wiping out remaining hope of Fed rate cuts. Markets are now pricing a 50% chance of a December rate hike, with hawkish Fed Chair Kevin Warsh adding conviction to a stagflationary outlook driven by the near-shutdown of the Strait of Hormuz.

headline: HEMLO MINING HITS 16.1 G/T GOLD OVER 8.1 METRES IN NEW SOUTH-RIM ZONE; BONANZA INTERVAL REACHES 59.7 G/T
snippet: Hemlo Mining Corp. reported high-grade gold assays from its newly interpreted South-Rim Zone at the historic Ontario Hemlo mine on May 14, with drill hole 7652606 returning 16.1 g/t Au over 8.1m including a 2m bonanza interval of 59.7 g/t. All seven holes completed in the 20-hole South-Rim program intersected mineralization — results from a 130,000m exploration campaign marking the deposit's first full year of drilling since Carcetti Capital acquired it from Barrick for approximately $1.1B (C$1.5B) last fall.

headline: PENTAGON-BACKED RARE EARTHS ON FIRE: UAMY UP 274% YTD, $354M IN CONTRACTS; CRML EYES WORLD'S BIGGEST EX-CHINA DEPOSIT
snippet: U.S. Antimony (UAMY) is up 274% year-to-date on 163% revenue growth and $354M in signed Pentagon contracts, while Critical Metals Corp. (CRML) is advancing Tanbreez — potentially the world's largest non-Chinese rare earth deposit — as overlooked alternatives to MP Materials. Both names are benefiting from Project Vault, the Trump administration's $12B critical minerals initiative, as China controls 90–95% of global rare earth processing capacity.

headline: DOLLAR IS SHRINKING AND GOLD COULD EXPLODE HIGHER — M2 UP 4.9% YoY, PPI PRINTS HOTTEST IN 4 YEARS
snippet: Money Metals Exchange argues gold is poised for an explosive move as M2 money supply grew 4.9% year-over-year to $22.67 trillion — a 'real' inflation rate that exposes the inadequacy of official CPI figures. A 6% PPI print, the hottest in nearly four years, landed on a market Money Metals says has been preparing for the wrong policy regime, with the inflationary reality now impossible for the Fed to ignore.

headline: BARRICK SMASHES Q1 WITH 238% EARNINGS SURGE; LAUNCHES $3B BUYBACK AND PLANS NORTH AMERICAN IPO
snippet: Barrick Mining crushed its own Q1 2026 guidance with 719,000 oz of gold produced — well above its 640,000–680,000 oz range — while adjusted EPS surged 180% to $0.98 and attributable free cash flow hit $1.21B. The board approved a new $3B share buyback and signalled plans for a North American IPO of its gold assets, with full-year guidance reiterated at 2.9–3.25M oz at AISC of $1,760–$1,950/oz.

headline: MINING M&A WAVE ROLLS ON: BLOOMBERG FLAGS ANOTHER GOLD DEAL AS Q1 2026 TRANSACTIONS TOTAL $21.6B
snippet: Bloomberg's mining newsletter flagged yet another deal closing in the gold sector on May 13 as Q1 2026 logged 121 transactions worth $21.6B — a 34% jump in value over Q1 2025 and the fastest-paced start to a year since 2023. Over 77% of deal value has been concentrated in gold and silver assets, with Zijin's C$5.5B friendly bid for Allied Gold among the largest pending closings as its May 29 outside date approaches.

headline: COPPER SMASHES ALL-TIME HIGH AT $13,943/T BEFORE INFLATION SELLOFF; J.P. MORGAN SEES 330K-TONNE DEFICIT
snippet: LME copper set a new closing record of $13,943/t on May 11 — up more than 40% year-over-year — as AI data center demand collided with sulfur supply disruptions from the near-closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which analysts estimate could affect as much as 4.8M tonnes of copper output globally. J.P. Morgan forecasts a 330,000-tonne refined copper deficit in 2026, though the metal retreated in the broad May 15 inflation-driven selloff.

headline: LITHIUM MARKET POISED FOR 25% GROWTH IN 2026 AS BATTERY STORAGE DEMAND SURGES TO 31% OF TOTAL CONSUMPTION
snippet: Battery energy storage systems are reshaping the lithium demand picture — their share of global lithium consumption is projected to jump from 23% in 2025 to 31% in 2026, driving total market growth that could reach 25% for the year. China lithium carbonate prices surged 78% in just over a month off multi-year lows, while Zimbabwe's export ban on raw lithium concentrate and structural supply constraints add fresh upward pressure.

headline: URANIUM SPOT AT $101/LB ON PATH TO $120-140 AS NEXGEN AND DENISON BREAK GROUND ON CANADIAN MINES
snippet: Uranium spot prices hit a year-to-date high of $101.41/lb in late January and are consolidating as term prices converge toward the $120–140 range in Q1 2026 market analysis. On the supply side, NexGen Energy's Rook I — Canada's largest development-stage uranium deposit at ~30M lb/year capacity — and Denison Mines' Phoenix project are both entering construction this summer, the first new Canadian uranium mines to break ground in over a decade.

headline: PRINCE SILVER GRADUATES TO OTCQX BEST MARKET AS COMPANY TARGETS MAIDEN NI 43-101 RESOURCE ESTIMATE BY YEAR-END
snippet: Prince Silver Corp. (CSE: PRNC, OTCQX: PRNCF) upgraded from OTCQB to the OTCQX Best Market on May 14, broadening U.S. investor access as the company advances its silver-gold-critical minerals project toward a maiden NI 43-101 resource estimate targeted by end of 2026. CEO Derek Iwanaka cited the OTCQX graduation as a key step in raising the company's institutional profile ahead of the resource milestone.

headline: BP SILVER OUTLINES 2026 EXPLORATION PROGRAM AT BOLIVIA'S COSUÑO PROJECT; MULTI-TARGET SAMPLING NOW UNDERWAY
snippet: BP Silver Corp. (TSXV: BPAG, OTCQB: BPSCF) has commenced geochemical sampling, geological mapping, and road construction at its Cosuño Silver Project in Bolivia, with work advancing across multiple target areas in what the company calls its most active exploration season to date. The 2026 program builds on first-ever drill results recently released from Cosuño, where BP Silver is targeting a large-scale silver system.

headline: GOLD STOCKS CORRECTION IN PROGRESS — GOLDSEEK ANALYSTS SEARCH FOR THE LOW AS EQUITIES LAG BULLION
snippet: GoldSeek analysts map the ongoing correction in gold mining equities, which have lagged physical bullion during gold's historic run to $5,595/oz earlier in 2026 — and now face added pressure after the May 15 inflation-driven selloff dragged gold back below $4,600. The piece identifies where the sector may find technical support and argues the pullback presents a potential accumulation window ahead of an eventual re-rating as miners catch up to near-record gold prices.
